description: Liminal is a team driven by curiosity, creativity, and the desire to explore the unknown. Bringing together our passion for space, engineering, robotics, and technology, we aim to turn ambitious ideas into meaningful solutions. We believe innovation begins at the boundary between what we know and what we have yet to discover.
summary: We developed ARES Mars 3D, an interactive, browser-based 3D Martian terrain visualization and autonomous mission-planning platform built on the IAU 2000 Areoid reference datum.   Mars has zero GPS satellites, no global magnetic field for compass navigation, and steep crater cliffs up to 24° that appear flat on traditional 2D orbital maps. ARES addresses this challenge by transforming real planetary elevation and spectral datasets—covering landing sites like Jezero, Gale, and Chryse—into a real-time 3D mission control environment. Using a slope-weighted A* pathfinding algorithm, the platform detects terrain hazards and computes safe, energy-efficient rover routes around impassable cliffs. It also integrates 10 mission modules, including 3D Dive, AI Brief, Subsystems telemetry, Sol & Optics day/night simulation, EVA & RF astronaut communication analysis, and an interactive Astronaut Visor HUD with LIBS laser rock analysis.   Because the 4-to-24-minute signal delay between Earth and Mars prevents real-time joystick control, ARES is vital as an accessible, zero-install decision-support tool for validating safe daily traverses while making real planetary data interactive for researchers, students, and future explorers.
details:
ARES Mars 3D is an interactive, browser-based 3D Martian terrain visualization and autonomous mission-planning platform built on the IAU 2000 Areoid datum. Because Mars has no GPS satellites, no global magnetic field, and steep crater cliffs up to 24° hidden by traditional 2D maps, mission planners face severe navigation risks.

  • How It Works: Using real planetary elevation and spectral datasets (modeled after NASA’s MOLA, HiRISE DEM, and CRISM) across sites like Jezero, Gale, and Chryse, our custom slope-weighted A* pathfinding algorithm calculates safe, energy-efficient rover routes around impassable terrain. Users can explore 10 integrated modules—including 3D Dive, Hazards, AI Brief, Rover & Crew, Subsystems, Sol & Optics, and EVA & RF—alongside interactive Astronaut Visor HUD, LIBS Laser, and simulation game modes.
  • Benefits & Impact: With a 4-to-24-minute signal delay between Earth and Mars, ARES acts as an accessible, zero-install decision-support tool for planning safe rover traverses, analyzing astronaut radio coverage, and bringing planetary science to students and researchers.
  • Tech Stack & Design: Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js / WebGL, and deployed on Vercel. Our team prioritized physical realism (24° slope limits), smooth browser performance without specialized GPUs, and a 12-step guided interface that blends engineering simulation with hands-on exploration.
